title: Half Your EV's Highway Energy Goes to THIS 💨⚡ #shorts

scenes.text: At highway speed, roughly half your car's energy goes into one thing: pushing air.
Drag grows with the square of speed. Double your speed, and the air pushes back four times harder.
And since you cover ground twice as fast, the power needed goes up eight times.
So engineers chase the drag coefficient. A boxy SUV: about zero point four. An average car: under zero point three.
The Mercedes EQS: just zero point two zero.
That's why EVs get flush handles, smooth wheels, and a closed front.
In an EV, shape is range. Would you trade looks for miles? Follow EV Drive for daily car tech.
